label: EDPB Guidelines 3/2019 — Processing through Video Devices
body: • Photographs and video are not automatically biometric data — they become Art. 9 biometric only when processed through a specific technical means that allows unique identification (template extraction, face matching against a database).
• A plain photograph in an HR file = ordinary personal data; the same photograph processed through facial-recognition templating = Art. 9 special category data.
• Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)) is the most common basis for CCTV — but balancing test is strict, especially in public-facing or workplace contexts.
• Mandatory: signage / on-the-spot first-layer notice + a full second-layer notice available on request.
• Retention: short by default (24–72 hours typical); longer requires documented justification.

• Subject-rights operations: access requests can be unique — controllers may need to provide a still image or footage clip, subject to third-party redaction. DPIA generally required for systematic monitoring of public areas (Art. 35(3)(c)).
